system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Position-wise support normalisation of MVFA's branches
SUMMARY: Normalise each branch's patch score by the leave-one-out support scores at the same grid position, shrunk towards the global support statistic, so anatomy-driven offsets are removed without test-set statistics.
HYPOTHESIS: On spatially aligned modalities (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, OCT17), position-wise normalisation improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles at K >= 4, and it is not worse than global percentiles on ChestXray and HIS by more than 0.5 points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; global support percentiles; position-wise support normalisation). For branch b, level l and position j: mu_j, sd_j from the K LOO support scores at j (and its 3x3 neighbourhood), shrunk: mu*_j = (n mu_j + 20 mu_g)/(n + 20), likewise sd; z = (s_j - mu*_j)/sd*_j, mapped by a logistic to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, false-positive rate in normal images per position (heat map), per-image score shift.
RATIONALE: Medical images of one modality are roughly aligned, and ADAN shows that much of an adapted CLIP map reflects anatomy. A single global normaliser per branch therefore mixes positions where normal anatomy scores high (e.g., skull, retinal layers) with positions where it scores low. Normalising each grid position by the support-normal scores at that position (shrunk towards the global statistic because K is small) removes anatomy-driven offsets inductively, before the unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: positional_refs(support_maps) computes per-position LOO statistics with a 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage weight 20. 2) test_few.py: per-image positional z-scores per branch and level, logistic map, 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: neighbourhood 3x3, shrinkage 20 (ablation {5, 20, 80}); no training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, positional false-positive maps, score shift. Ablations: shrinkage; neighbourhood size. Falsified if no pixel-AUROC gain on aligned modalities.

Idea B:
TITLE: Source-episode scale with support re-centring for inductive MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Learn each branch's scale on simulated few-shot episodes from the source modalities and set only its location from the K target supports, replacing test-set min-max.
HYPOTHESIS: At K = 2, the source-episode scale with support re-centring loses at least 1 AUROC point less than the support-percentile normaliser relative to the transductive pipeline, and at K >= 4 both are within 1 point of it.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; support percentiles; source-episode scale + support location). On each source modality's validation split, 50 episodes of K normal supports and 40 queries; for branch b, z_b = (s_b - mu_supp,b) / sigma_b, where mu_supp,b is the median LOO support patch score of the episode and sigma_b is fitted across episodes as the median absolute deviation of normal query patch scores around mu_supp,b. On the target only mu_supp,b is computed. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, per-image score shift.
RATIONALE: Support statistics from K normal images are noisy for small K. MVFA is trained on five source modalities with validation splits, so the SCALE of each branch can be learned there from simulated few-shot episodes and transferred, while only the LOCATION is set on the target from its K supports. This keeps the 0.5 fusion and max pooling and separates a stable learned scale from a cheap per-modality shift.
METHOD: 1) calibrate_episodes.py: for each training fold, sample episodes on source validation splits using the trained model's scoring functions; estimate sigma_b per branch and level; save calib.json. 2) test_few.py: per-image z_b with mu from the target supports (LOO) and sigma from calib.json; then the unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: 50 episodes, 40 queries, K matched to the target K; no adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, score shift. Falsified if the source-episode scale is not better than support percentiles at K = 2.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
